A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MAS-Orchestra and MASBench study and contain readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–H. Matching reflowed content and checking rendered graphics supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original controlled MAS–SAS experiments and public-benchmark evaluations in Sections 5–6, with supplementary analyses and measured inference costs in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: v5 retains those original experiments, including the benchmark accuracies in Table 3, supplementary analyses in Appendix C, and inference measurements in Table D.2.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices F–H retain the same holistic function-calling orchestration, DoM configurations, GRPO training, sub-agent implementations, and parsers. The DebateAgent correction changes only a heading.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same five-axis MASBench coverage derived from iGSM/RULER, the same training sources, and the same AIME24, AIME25, GPQA, HotpotQA, and BrowseComp+ evaluations.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains the same standalone agents and orchestration comparators, including AFlow, MaAS, MAS-GPT, ToolOrchestra, GPT-5, and Claude-Sonnet-4.5. MAS-Zero’s failure entry and comparator membership in supplementary comparisons also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices A–D retain the same splits, sample sizes, training budgets, model configurations, correctness evaluation, and task-specific DoM settings. No experiments or revised protocols are introduced.

E4.justification: The adversarial-training comparisons, separate versus combined training, orchestrator-size controls, complexity generalization, reasoning-effort/context analyses, and case studies in Appendix C are unchanged. Appendix D retains the same orchestration and cost analyses.

E5.justification: Avg@8 reporting in Table 3 and the figures is unchanged. Neither version adds or revises run/seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedures, or significance tests relative to the other.

E6.justification: The numerical entries and plotted findings match throughout. For example, Table 3 retains MAS-Orchestra’s 66.25 on AIME24 and 65.21 on GPQA, and Table D.2 retains the same inference-cost measurements.

T1.justification: The MAS/DoM formulation, five-axis definitions, reward and objective equations (1)–(4), and GRPO expressions (5)–(7) are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about holistic RL orchestration, MASBench, conditional MAS benefits, benchmark performance, and efficiency.

C2.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices C–D preserve the same interpretations and qualifications concerning task structure, model capability, adversarial training, context limits, and differences from baselines’ original training environments.

D1.justification: v3’s first page provides one project-page link; v5 updates that address and adds direct links for the live demo, MASBench dataset, and code repository. This expands access documentation, while implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, Table 1, Appendix E, and the reference list retain the same cited works and research positioning. The updated publication notice concerns this paper’s metadata.

P1.justification: v5 replaces the preprint notice with ICML 2026 proceedings information and corrects “DebateaAgent” to “DebateAgent” in Appendix G.3. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Four resource icons and an expanded title-page link block change the front-page layout and cause subsequent text and figure reflow. Existing scientific figures and tables retain their designs, captions, and contents.

improvement.justification: The direct code and MASBench links improve resource discoverability from the PDF, and the appendix heading correction provides a small editorial benefit. These are limited documentation gains; the methods, experimental evidence, interpretations, and limitations remain unchanged.
